headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 17 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: The final chance for the sprinters? Some still eye a potential opportunity in Granada, on the final day of La Vuelta 26. To earn a final sprint, they would need to survive the climb of the Alhambra, while today’s stage is more straightforward: 185 kilometres of racing on flat roads between Dos Hermanas and Seville, with barely 1,000 metres of elevation gain. The neutral start is set at 13:00, the start proper at 13:24 after an 11.2 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Dos Hermanas makes its debut as a La Vuelta stage town
subtext: Dos Hermanas has been the setting of Vuelta a Andalucia stages a handful of times in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: Happy birthday Lenny
subtext: Lennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek) turns 30 today. The German breakaway expert takes part in his third La Vuelta and won stage 9 of the 2023 edition between Cartagena and Collado de la Cruz de Caravaca. Today is also the birth date of Rik Van Steenbergen, a 3-time world champion and winner of six stages in his first and only La Vuelta participation (1956). He passed away in 2003.

headline: Riders with 4+ stages in their first La Vuelta

The others had already done the Tour de France or Giro d’Italia.

headline: Let’s roll

headline: La Roja
subtext: Despite the wind and the tension, stage 16 brought no change at the top of the overall standings. Enric Mas (Movistar) still leads with a gap of 2’06’’ to Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) (+2’06’’), and 2’10’’ to Primoz Roglic (+2’10’’).

headline: Green jersey
subtext: With a place of 6th while leading out Matthew Brennan to victory in La Rabida, Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) pushed his tally to 282 points, against 189 for his British teammate. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) is still third with 153 points. A rider can grab a maximum of 220 points in the five final stages, including 70 today (50 at the finish, 20 at the intermediate sprint).

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) still leads the mountains standings with 69 points, a tally that gives him a significant margin on Wout van Aert (40 points). Enric Mas (Movistar) follows with 24 points. There are 53 points up for grabs this week, but they’re all packed in stages 19 (20 points) and 20 (33 points).

headline: Team standings

headline: Last dance for the baroudeurs?
subtext: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) made it clear yesterday: "Then there’s the time trial, two mountain stages and the finish." The French baroudeur has been one of the most active riders in LaVuelta 26, along with his breakaway companion today, Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH). "One day it’s going to work out", the Spaniard said yesterday.

headline: Can Cofidis flip the script?
subtext: Second to Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) on stages 11 and 16, Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) is looking for an opening to double his tally after winning stage 8 in Xeraco. He knows the way to the win in Seville: he dominated the sprint on stage 4 of the 2017 Vuelta a Andalucia here. “[Matthew Brennan] is the fastest rider in this Vuelta; he’s already shown that", Coquard's lead-out man Alexis Renard said this morning. "His team is also the strongest, with a superb lead-out for him in the form of Wout van Aert. There’s not much we can do. Today we’ll see what tactics to put in place to go for first place. [Bryan Coquard] finished fourth two years ago; it’s not at all the same stage or the same finale, but it’s the same finish line, so we’ll try to do better. I hope to do everything I can to go for first place today. It would be great to finish on that note and secure a good placing in the final sprint.”

headline: Cofidis pull the bunch with Visma-Lease a Bike
subtext: So far, Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) has been the only sprinter to find an opening against Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) in La Vuelta 26.

headline: Macias: "We’re pleased, happy and excited"
subtext: César Macías (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) secured his first top-10 finish in a Grand Tour stage yesterday: “I’m quite pleased with myself, and so is the team. I think it was a great result yesterday to finish in the top ten in a Grand Tour, given that it is my debut. We’re pleased, happy and excited about today as well. The truth is today I’ve got that desire to improve, that hunger to keep fighting. I think today is the last chance for the sprinters, so we’re going to make the most of this final opportunity 100 per cent. Well, there can always be a surprise; a breakaway might form – we don’t know – but ultimately we know that Visma also have a very strong team to control the race.”

headline: The gap is down to 3'10''
subtext: The peloton are at km 53 with Cofidis and Visma-Lease a Bike at the helm.

headline: Brennan, inspired by Gaviria and the Maillot Jaune
subtext: The last sprinter with four stage wins in his debut Grand Tour was Fernando Gaviria in the Giro 2017. The Colombian sprinter then claimed the first Maillot Jaune of the Tour de France 2018. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) dreams of following in his footsteps with a UK Grand Départ next year: “I already said to the team two years ago now, when I heard about a UK start, I’d really like to be there on start line and to have guys like Wout [van Aert] and Christophe [Laporte] there also. We can really try to replicate what we do here into a Yellow Jersey on day 1.”

headline: 3'05'' at km 60
subtext: The biggest gap recorded so far was 4'30'' at km 18.

headline: Küng: "I will focus more on tomorrow"
subtext: Stefan Küng (Tudor) was 5th in Seville in La Vuelta 24... But the Swiss has his mind set on tomorrow's stage: “With the TT, I don't wanna take any risk. I remember the day I was fifth [stage 5 of La Vuelta 24, finishing in Seville], it was the first week of the Vuelta, I was feeling good, three km to go it was a straight line, Kevin Geniets moved me up, I was put in position and I did the rest, but today there is more to lose than to win. I will focus more on tomorrow. You can never count Wout van Aert out. Ethan Hayter can beat everyone on a good day. And also many other guys who can ride fast. It’s up to me tomorrow.”

headline: Cofidis drive the bunch on their own
subtext: Bryan Coquard has four teammates at the front of the peloton, while Brennan's have dropped back.

headline: Soon in Alcala de Guadaira, already linked to Seville and Ewan in La Vuelta history
subtext: Seville left a spectacular mark in the history of La Vuelta when it hosted the Gran Salida in 2010 with a team time trial at night. HTC-Columbia won the stage and Mark Cavendish became the first wearer of La Roja, as the red leader’s jersey was introduced that year, replacing the “maillot de oro” (golden jersey). The next day, the race started from Alcala de Guadaira (km 105.8 on today’s route), also home to the finish of stage 5 of La Vuelta 15. Aged 21, Caleb Ewan took his first Grand Tour stage win.

headline: Seville, from 1935 to 2024
subtext: Sevilla was already a stage city in the very first edition of La Vuelta, in 1935. Belgium’s Gustaaf Deloor asserted his dominance on the race as he took the victory while already leading the overall standings. The most recent winner in Seville is Pavel Bittner, who outsprinted Wout van Aert and Kaden Groves on stage 5 of La Vuelta 24. Bryan Coquard and Stefan Küng completed the day’s top 5. Two riders from Sevilla have won stages in La Vuelta: - Antonio Montes, 3 stage wins across the 1935, 1941 and 1945 editions - Antonio Piedra, 1 stage win in 2012 (Lagos de Covadonga) In the outskirts of Seville, Tomares hosted the finish of stage 16 of La Vuelta 22. Remco Evenepoel was wearing La Roja; Primoz Roglic attacked in the finale but he was caught in a crash within the final 500 metres. Mads Pedersen won the stage. Roglic didn’t start the next day.

headline: Brennan: "We just have to follow the plan"
subtext: Did Wout van Aert explain to Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) the finish in Seville where he finished 2nd in 2024? “Yes, the video was played in the Whatsapp chat this morning, and then he explained the finish a bit, and then he said: ‘I went too early, and also I launched for the line too early’; and Pavel [Bittner] did a good ride to come around him. So hopefully we can change it this year on the same finish, but it’s good that he knows the course a bit." "It's gonna be pretty fast and I think there’s gonna be a lot of guys who want to be up the front, so it does change a lot", the British sprinter continued. "It adds a lot of chaos and there’s gonna be a lot of guys who shouldn’t be there or aren’t normally there, to give a bit of a try to help their teammates to try and do their best opportunity they can in the sprint. So we just have to work a way around that and follow the plan that we have.”

headline: The gap decreases again
subtext: The peloton have covered 100 kilometres and they trail by 430''.

headline: Visma-Lease a Bike on the hunt for a 7th stage win
subtext: The Dutch team have proved dominant on flat and rolling stages of La Vuelta 26 with four stage wins for Matthew Brennan and two four Wout van Aert. Van they make it seven and match UAE Emirates XRG’s record from 2025? “I’ve lost count, we’ve won so many!”, an elated Brennan said yesterday. “Seven stage wins is something that happens very rarely”, Van Aert observed. “We are very proud with six already, but with the legs and the team spirit we have, we keep trying.”

headline: Camprubi: "I try to read the finish"
subtext: What does Marcel Camprubí (Pinarello-Q36.5) think of when he thinks of Seville? “I think, ‘Sevilla tiene un color especial’ [Seville has a special colour], as the song goes. I think it’s a very beautiful city. I think of flamenco, above all, and the culture of the people.” The Spanish champion finished 11th yesterday in the La Rabida sprint: “You’ve got to reinvent yourself! No, I think it was a very technical sprint; it wasn’t so much about leg strength. And as, unfortunately, our sprinter David González had to withdraw, we were told to give it a go, and I managed to get in there. All in all, I’m happy with this result. I think it’s great to practise these finishes too, because they give you skills that can even come in handy for other types of races later on. I reckon today’s going to be more dangerous. It’ll be an easier day, with far more people getting involved. I’m going to try and read the finish a bit, and if I see I can get in there, I’ll go for it, but today I’m not as confident as I was yesterday.”

headline: Hofstetter: "Brennan ruined my chances"
subtext: Hugo Hofstetter (NSN) explained at the start he is out for revenge after getting tangled up with Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) in La Rabida: “Yesterday was the day I was most disappointed. I put in a huge effort after the roundabout, I didn’t take any risks, I came back well on the outside of the final left-hand bend, I was right on Coquard’s wheel and Brennan’s wheel hit my shoe. He ruined my shoe and all my chances because I lost my trajectory; I had to find my pedal again, so my sprint was ruined. But I came back strong, so I have regrets when I think of the legs I had. I was in an ideal position, so I was very disappointed yesterday. Today, in a sprint like this, there’ll be a lot of waiting around and you’ll need to be very patient on the wide avenues; riders can come from the back and, with a wave of riders, it’s always possible, in the slipstream, to pull away at the last moment.”
